chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from one of our companions, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The man, when he sees the crescent of Dhi al-Qadah, and he intends the going, should neither take (hair) from his head not from his beard.

key_terms.الْخُرُوجَ: The going, referring to the departure for pilgrimage (Hajj or Umrah).
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhi al-Qadah, the tenth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, marking the beginning of the Hajj season.
key_terms.رَأْسِهِ: His head, referring to the hair on the scalp.
key_terms.لِحْيَتِهِ: His beard, referring to the facial hair.

ai.seo_question: When does a pilgrim stop cutting their hair before Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies that the prohibition on cutting hair for the Muhrim begins upon sighting the crescent of Dhi al-Qadah, marking the start of the Hajj season rather than the actual departure. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the lunar calendar's role in defining the sanctity of the pilgrimage months, ensuring the Muhrim enters the state of Ihram with the prescribed physical signs of consecration already in place.
